basic.a: An all-on-chain Web4 protocol that coordinates computing power and traffic, distributing value strictly through rules.

basic.q: How is Web4 different from Web3?
basic.a: Web3 secures ownership; Web4 focuses on large-scale coordination and automated execution.

basic.q: What's the difference between WANT and XANT?
basic.a: WANT is the ecosystem token and settlement unit. XANT is a “seed” credential used to ignite the computing engine.

organization.q: How do I qualify for a star tier?
organization.a: You must meet requirements on effective addresses, performance, and your own capacity.

organization.q: Is a higher star tier always better?
organization.a: Higher tiers come with higher responsibility and higher capacity requirements.

organization.q: Do I have to do offline outreach?
organization.a: Not necessarily. Online channels, content, and community growth can all work.

organization.q: What is the Tier-1 (T1) engine for?
organization.a: To lower the onboarding barrier and improve conversion for new users.

organization.q: Can I gift engines to downlines?
organization.a: Yes—so long as it stays within the protocol’s capacity/carrying rules.

organization.q: Does a bigger organization automatically mean more profit?

organization.q: Does a bigger network mean bigger pressure?
